subject.title: Feature request: first-class async result routing back to originating topic sessions

question: Should OpenClaw own a first-class async callback-route contract in core, expose only the missing plugin/Gateway seams, or leave this as workspace/plugin-owned automation?
rationale: The requested capability is useful but spans core storage, plugin APIs, Gateway ingress, session routing, visible delivery, privacy, and approval policy, so implementation should not start before maintainers choose the product boundary.

options.title: Design plugin/Gateway seam first
options.body: Define the smallest stable route API or plugin hook that lets external watchers register, match, dedupe, deliver, and wake topic sessions without committing core to a broad orchestration registry.

options.title: Own a core route registry
options.body: Build a Gateway-managed SQLite-backed route registry and accept core ownership for lifecycle, migrations, privacy, matching, ambiguity handling, and approval policy.

options.title: Keep it workspace/plugin-owned
options.body: Close or defer the core feature and document how to assemble the workflow from hooks, Task Flow, targeted wake, and plugin code.

recommendation.title: Design plugin/Gateway seam first
recommendation.body: Define the smallest stable route API or plugin hook that lets external watchers register, match, dedupe, deliver, and wake topic sessions without committing core to a broad orchestration registry.

likelyOwner.reason: The main unresolved question is the product/API boundary, and this owner has recent vision/docs and routing-adjacent history.
